title: Time Taken to Mark All Nodes
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and edges defined by a 2D integer array, determine the time for each node to be marked.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and edges defined by a 2D integer array, determine the time for each node to be marked. If a node is odd-numbered, it will get marked at time x if there is at least one adjacent node that was marked at time x - 1 . If a node is even-numbered, it will get marked at time x if there is at least one adjacent node that was marked at time x - 2 . Return an array where each element times[i] represents the time when all nodes get marked, assuming node i is marked at time t = 0 .
constraints: edges describes a tree of 2–100,000 nodes numbered from zero.
Traversing into an odd node costs one time unit; traversing into an even node costs two.
For every possible initially marked node, return the maximum directed weighted distance to any node.
hints: Marking time along a path is the sum of entry costs of every node after the source.
Compute longest downward paths, then reroot while carrying the best path through parent or a sibling.
For each child use the parent entry cost plus max(parent-up, best other child branch).
The two passes partition every destination path by its first edge, so each source receives its exact weighted eccentricity.
editorial: The two passes partition every destination path by its first edge, so each source receives its exact weighted eccentricity.

tests.explanation: Starting at nodes 0,1,2 takes 2,4,3 time respectively to reach every node.
From zero, odd node one costs one; from one, even node zero costs two.
